result.topic_en: The page ends a remark that mathematical statements are as certain as arithmetic with whole numbers (with reference to Kant), lists two hydrodynamic problems about falling walls and wind pressure on a screen, and begins a note of something to say to Gordan.

items.english: 1) A horizontal wall falling under the influence of gravity, when the air is still and then when it moves somewhat (according to the experiments there is supposed to be a large difference. Prove this theoretically.)

items.quote:
2/ Holzgefäss d. h. Schirm {+erhält ziemlich+}
den gleichen Druck, wenn der Wind schief
stösst als wenn er grade kommt, während
bei der graden Wand die Sinuscurve gilt.
items.english: 2) A wooden vessel, i.e. a screen, receives roughly the same pressure when the wind strikes obliquely as when it comes straight on, whereas for the straight wall the sine curve holds.
